extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys and agents, IP strategists, general counsel, legal operations teams
extracted.subtask_description: Using examiner-level analytics, appeals intelligence, and automated alerts to choose the optimal prosecution path (interview, RCE, appeal, continuation, abandon, or prioritized Track One) and to standardize and accelerate decisions across counsel and business units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action decision at each office action (interview/RCE/appeal/abandon)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every office action is a fork in the road. Interview, RCE, appeal, or abandon. Track One or standard. Push now or pivot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the next move clear with examiner-level win rates, portfolio alerts, and prosecution dashboards; use data to decide when to escalate (appeal), seek interviews, file an RCE, or abandon. Standardize decisions so you cut actions, time, and money—not corners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate Track One (prioritized examination) ROI before paying
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate Track One and other USPTO programs before you spend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare expected pendency and outcomes by tech area and examiner to determine whether paying for faster prosecution is cost-effective; use the platform's Track One comparison to decide when acceleration is a smart investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use examiner-level win rates and examiners' behavior to predict outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Juristat makes the next move clear with examiner-level win rates, portfolio alerts, and a ready-to-use Prosecution Strategy dashboard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate examiner trends to craft strategies with precision and confidence by leveraging examiner, art-unit, and tech-center context from historical application data; apply these predictions when drafting arguments and choosing escalation paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface arguments and strategies from similar appeals and cases
rubrics_metrics.description: See what worked for others. Surface arguments, outcomes, and strategies from similar appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical appeal data and comparable cases to strengthen prosecution or appeal approaches; benchmark reversal patterns across similar cases using the Appeals Module to inform argument selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forecast prosecution outcomes and model prosecution cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Forecast prosecution outcomes and reduce uncertainty in filing, appeals, and global strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model spend and pick the cheapest winning path; use prosecution cost forecasting to decide whether to pursue amendments, RCEs, appeals, or other routes that balance cost with likelihood of allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect escalation opportunities and problematic prosecutions (long prosecutions, low-allowance examiners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Live signals surface where to act—interview, appeal, and continuation opportunities, long prosecutions, and low-allowance examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor dashboards and alerts to identify matters with excessive office actions or slow pendency and prioritize interventions for those files where data indicates higher risk or lower chance of allowance without escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set and enforce rules/alerts tied to examiner metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and alerts enforce when to push, pivot, or walk away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build if-then rules tied to examiner metrics (e.g., low allowance rate triggers review); share and export rules across matters to standardize decisions across attorneys and outside counsel and to align leadership quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use automated alerts for OA counts, RCE streaks, missed interviews, and other risk signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I set custom alerts for risky prosecutions? Yes. Trigger alerts on OA counts, RCE streaks, missed interviews, low-allowance examiners, and more—using thresholds you define.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define thresholds that reflect your risk tolerance and portfolio priorities; act on alerts to avoid wasted budget and to intervene before matters become protracted or costly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals benchmarking and monetization signals (reversal patterns, forward-citation momentum)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an appeal is in play, the Appeals Module benchmarks reversal patterns across similar cases; forward-citation momentum shows where to protect, license, or prune.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use benchmarks to estimate appeal success probability and use citation/market signals to make portfolio-level decisions (e.g., continue prosecution, monetize via licensing, or prune low-value assets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Create and export concise, data-backed briefs for escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: Exportable briefs align counsel and leadership the same day—so you choose the lowest-cost, highest-confidence path, consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize examiner metrics, comparable cases, and recommended actions in an exportable brief to ensure fast alignment across internal and external stakeholders during critical decision points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize playbooks and decision-making across examiners, firms, and business units
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize your playbook across examiners, firms, and business units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the platform to codify preferred responses and escalation criteria so that in-house and outside counsel make consistent, repeatable decisions that reduce variability and cost across the portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data coverage and freshness as a quality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Juristat’s industry-leading patent analytics database is based on more than 10 million applications. We examine USPTO data across pending, abandoned, and granted applications. Examiner, art unit, assignee, and firm metrics included. Historical coverage back to 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on automatically refreshed data to keep dashboards and alerts current; validate decisions using broad historical coverage and examiner-level granularity to avoid basing strategy on stale or incomplete datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerate prosecution and reduce office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce costly detours and move more patents to allowance with fewer office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ analytics-driven prosecution to identify the most effective interventions (e.g., interviews, claims amendments, appeals) earlier in the lifecycle to shorten prosecution and lower prosecution costs.
